cues.en: Sitcoms of the late eighties and early nineties were ruled by the laughter track, which had been a staple of American sitcoms since the nineteen fifties.
cues.zh: 八十年代末和九十年代初的情景喜剧由笑声轨主导，而笑声轨自五十年代以来一直是美国情景喜剧的标配。

cues.en: Originally provided by a live studio audience, but now it was just fake canned laughter, used as an artificial way to prop up lazy one liners and unimaginative quips. The problem with using laughter tracks is that they only allow for jokes to be structured in a very particular way with long lead ins and big punch lines. But there is also a forced quality to it too, as it takes the onus away from the audience and tells us when to react.
cues.zh: 它最初由现场演播室观众提供，但后来只剩下虚假的罐头笑声，被当作一种人为手段，来硬撑敷衍的单句笑话和缺乏想象力的俏皮话。使用笑声轨的问题在于，它只允许笑话按非常特定的方式构建：要有很长的铺垫和很大的包袱。但它也有一种强迫感，因为它把判断的责任从观众身上拿走，还告诉我们什么时候该反应。

cues.en: Now it has a purpose.
cues.zh: 现在它有目的了。

cues.en: The article also reveals another problem that was creeping its way into The Simpsons,
cues.zh: 这篇文章还揭示了另一个悄悄渗入《辛普森一家》的问题，

cues.en: and that is the two characters present here are not actually
cues.zh: 那就是，这里出现的两个角色其实并不是

cues.en: the same person.
cues.zh: 同一个人。

cues.en: One is the slow witted, downtrodden everyman from the first seven seasons,
cues.zh: 一个是前七季里那个迟钝、受尽欺压的普通人，

cues.en: and the other...
cues.zh: 而另一个……

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 呃，

cues.en: the other is jerkass Homer.
cues.zh: 另一个是混蛋荷马。

cues.en: Jerkass Homer is a term that's been coined to describe Homer of the modern era. While classic Homer is layered and nuanced,
cues.zh: “混蛋荷马”是个新造的词，用来形容现代版的荷马。经典荷马层次丰富、细腻微妙，

cues.en: jerk ass Homer is basically a wacky cartoon dad.
cues.zh: 而混蛋荷马基本上就是个古怪的卡通老爸。

cues.en: An indestructible
cues.zh: 一个打不死的、

cues.en: supremely confident sociopath
cues.zh: 极度自信的反社会人格，

cues.en: who's willing to leap headlong into any new venture for the most nonsensical
cues.zh: 为了最荒唐的

cues.en: of motives. There's little rhyme or reason to his actions, and the lens of satire was now being turned firmly inwards.
cues.zh: 动机就一头扎进任何新冒险。他的行为几乎毫无逻辑可言，而讽刺的视角如今也牢牢转向了内部。

cues.en: With many of Homer's jokes being lame, self referential one liners of a far weaker show.
cues.zh: Homer的许多笑话都成了蹩脚又自指的一句话段子，像来自一个差得多的节目。

cues.en: Pog machine?
cues.zh: Pog机器？

cues.en: Even I think this is crazy.
cues.zh: 连我都觉得这很疯狂。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: this shift could be felt not only in each member of the Simpsons family,
cues.zh: 这种转变不仅能在Simpsons一家每个成员身上感受到，

cues.en: but in every resident of Springfield,
cues.zh: 也能在Springfield每位居民身上感受到，

cues.en: sometimes completely destroying characters in the process.
cues.zh: 有时还在这过程中把角色彻底毁掉。

cues.en: Moe went from a violent lowlife vaguely criminal owner of a shady bar to a boring lovelorn family friend who only occasionally said the wrong thing. Lisa went from a skeptical, isolated intellectual and voice of reason to someone who religiously follows popular trends.
cues.zh: Moe从一个暴力底层、半带犯罪色彩的阴暗酒吧老板，变成了无聊、情场失意、只偶尔说错话的家庭朋友。Lisa从一个多疑孤立的知识分子和理性之声，变成了虔诚追随流行潮流的人。

cues.en: Or Barney who goes from an alcoholic to a
cues.zh: 又或者是 Barney，从一个酒鬼变成

cues.en: coffee drinker, turning him from a hilariously dark representation of a major societal woe into,
cues.zh: 一个爱喝咖啡的人，把他从对社会重大弊病的滑稽黑暗写照，变成，

cues.en: well, someone who likes coffee.
cues.zh: 嗯，一个喜欢咖啡的人。

cues.en: Every dark satirical edge of Springfield was being smoothed out and sterilized.
cues.zh: Springfield 的每一处黑暗讽刺锋芒，都在被磨平、消毒。

cues.en: Its characters were slowly devolving into simple minded cartoons of what they had once been. The exact kind of one dimensional writing Sam Simon had worked so hard to avoid.
cues.zh: 它的角色正慢慢退化成他们昔日形象的头脑简单漫画。正是 Sam Simon 努力避免的那种扁平化写作。

cues.en: The second major reason for the show's change
cues.zh: 这部剧转变的第二个主要原因

cues.en: is a little less tangible. The Simpsons was born out of a complete disdain for status quo, a hatred for the neutered zombified version of the American family that sitcoms of the late eighties depicted.
cues.zh: 则稍显无形。《辛普森一家》诞生于对现状的彻底蔑视，以及对八十年代末情景喜剧所描绘的那种被阉割、僵尸化的美国家庭的憎恶。

cues.en: And this anger gave the Simpsons its cynical edge it used to tear through pop culture of the time. But now, ten years later, The Simpsons was no longer a cruel and biting attack on popular media.
cues.zh: 这种愤怒赋予了《辛普森一家》愤世嫉俗的锋芒，让它得以撕开当时的流行文化。但十年后的现在，《辛普森一家》已不再是对大众媒体残酷而尖锐的攻击了。

cues.en: It was popular media. The pop culture landscape that the show had been created, Slampoon, had been utterly obliterated.
cues.zh: 它曾是大众媒体。这部剧诞生时所处的流行文化版图——Slampoon——已被彻底抹去。

cues.en: And in doing so,
cues.zh: 而这样一来，

cues.en: The Simpsons lost its ability to truly be satire.
cues.zh: The Simpsons 失去了真正作为讽刺作品的能力。

cues.en: Characters that had been conceived as a harsh critique of TV stereotypes of the time now lost all context.
cues.zh: 那些最初被构思为对当时电视刻板印象进行尖锐批判的角色，如今完全失去了语境。

cues.en: And The Simpsons itself was even being parodied by newer shows like Family Guy and South Park.
cues.zh: 而 The Simpsons 本身甚至开始被 Family Guy 和 South Park 等新剧恶搞。

cues.en: The Simpsons as a show had aged out, and as a result, it needed to transform
cues.zh: 作为一档节目，The Simpsons 已经过时，因此它需要转型

cues.en: and change its identity to stay relevant.
cues.zh: 并改变自身定位以保持相关性。

cues.en: And it did so in the most disappointing way possible.
cues.zh: 而且它是以最令人失望的方式做到的。

cues.en: And that was that rather than treating the idea of celebrity with the wry disdain it had in its earlier seasons,
cues.zh: 那就是：它不再像早期季那样，对名人这个概念带着一种嘲讽式的鄙夷，

cues.en: modern Simpsons revels in the celebration of the rich and famous.
cues.zh: 现代版《辛普森一家》反而沉醉于对富豪名流的追捧。

cues.en: No longer were bespoke guest characters created for each new celebrity, the joke now was just let the Simpsons meet a celebrity and have that serve as the gag.
cues.zh: 不再为每位新名人量身定制客串角色，现在的笑点只是让辛普森一家见个名人，然后把这当成包袱。

cues.en: And the result is some of the weakest, most insincere writing of the entire show.
cues.zh: 结果就是整部剧里最乏力、最不真诚的一些写作。

cues.en: Welcome to The United Kingdom. Prime Minister Tony Blair?
cues.zh: 欢迎来到英国。首相 Tony Blair？

cues.en: Hey, Blick one eighty two. Thanks for the lift, Tony Hawk. I gotta go now, Tony Hawk. Bart,
cues.zh: 嘿，Blick 182。谢谢你捎我一程，Tony Hawk。我现在得走了，Tony Hawk。Bart，

cues.en: you know Tony Hawk? Is this really the same show that so thoroughly took apart celebrity centric culture in episodes like Radioactive Man, Bart Gets Famous and The B Sharps?
cues.zh: 你认识 Tony Hawk 吗？这真的是那部在《Radioactive Man》《Bart Gets Famous》和《The B Sharps》等剧集里，把以名人为中心的文化如此彻底拆解的同一部剧吗？

cues.en: And the answer is no,
cues.zh: 答案是否定的，

cues.en: it's not.
cues.zh: 不是。

cues.en: This is no longer a show that satirizes pop culture.
cues.zh: 这已经不再是一部讽刺流行文化的剧了。

cues.en: This is one that actively worships it. The only thing that The Simpsons was a parody of now
cues.zh: 而这一部却对它顶礼膜拜。《辛普森一家》如今唯一还在恶搞的对象

cues.en: was The Simpsons.
cues.zh: 就是它自己。

cues.en: And this is the state it would remain in for the next two decades.
cues.zh: 而它接下来二十年都将停留在这个状态。

cues.en: A soulless, shambling husk that only vaguely resembles what it had once been.
cues.zh: 一具没有灵魂、步履蹒跚的空壳，只隐约还像它曾经的样子。

cues.en: And this is the period known
cues.zh: 而这个时期后来被称作

cues.en: as Zombie Simpsons.
cues.zh: “僵尸辛普森”。

cues.en: And so with this in mind,
cues.zh: 那么，带着这些认识，

cues.en: let's return to our graph and put all this together. The Simpsons was born in the last breath of the eighties and quickly became the dominant force of early nineties television
cues.zh: 让我们回到图表，把这一切串起来。《辛普森一家》诞生于八十年代的最后气息中，并迅速成为九十年代初电视的主导力量

cues.en: with a ferociously
cues.zh: 凭借一种极其猛烈

cues.en: satirical slant on not only entertainments,
cues.zh: 的讽刺视角，不仅针对娱乐，

cues.en: but also society itself.
cues.zh: 也针对社会本身。

cues.en: With masterfully written episodes and characters that drew in a global audience,
cues.zh: 凭借精妙编剧的剧集和角色，吸引了全球观众，

cues.en: thus creating Simpsons Mania right up until season eight where major staff changes
cues.zh: 由此掀起“辛普森狂热”，一直持续到第八季，此时主创团队的大变动

cues.en: slowly began to eke away at the identity and craft that made the show great. Slowly, little pieces of the Simpsons began falling away, with characters that were beginning to only vaguely resemble
cues.zh: 开始慢慢侵蚀让这部剧出色的特质与匠心。渐渐地，《辛普森一家》的一些细节开始流失，角色也开始只隐约像

cues.en: who they had once been,
cues.zh: 他们曾经的样子，

cues.zh: 到第九季的《校长与贫民》时达到了临界点。

cues.en: And thus, the show begins relying more and more on outlandish plots and absurd
cues.zh: 于是，这部剧开始越来越依赖离奇的情节和荒诞的

cues.en: self referential writing. Until season twelve, when now a decade away from the media landscape it had been created as a response to, the show ages out, and in an effort to stay relevant,
cues.zh: 自我指涉的写作。直到第十二季，此时距离它当初作为回应而诞生的媒体环境已过去十年，剧集逐渐过时，而为了保持相关性，

cues.en: transforms its relationship with pop culture. And in doing so, snuffed out the final spark that made The Simpsons what it was. And so
cues.zh: 改变了自己与流行文化的关系。而这么做，也掐灭了让 The Simpsons 成为其自身的最后火花。于是

cues.en: zombie Simpsons is born,
cues.zh: 僵尸辛普森诞生了，

cues.en: which would cause the legendary series to fall into decline that is still happening today, bottoming out at its most recent season twenty eight with the lowest ratings of the series' entire history.
cues.zh: 这导致这部传奇剧集陷入至今仍在持续的衰落，并在最近的第28季触底，创下全剧历史最低收视率。

cues.en: Ultimately,
cues.zh: 说到底，

cues.en: it's hard not to feel sad about what's happened to The Simpsons.
cues.zh: 看到 The Simpsons 变成今天这样，很难不感到难过。

cues.en: But even if the same staff had stayed on, even if everything had remained exactly the same for the show internally,
cues.zh: 但即便原班人马都留了下来，即便这部剧内部一切都保持原样，

cues.en: I think Simpsons was too much of a time that it could never really have survived the turn of the millennium.
cues.zh: 我觉得 The Simpsons 太属于它那个时代了，它根本不可能真正挺过千禧年之交。

cues.en: So much of it was so rooted in the culture of the nineties and its media, and I think that's okay.
cues.zh: 它太多东西都深深扎根于九十年代的文化和当时的媒体，我觉得这没什么问题。

cues.en: I think entertainment isn't meant to last forever, rather it's an extension of the people
cues.zh: 我觉得娱乐本来就不是为了永存的，它更像是创造它的那些人、

cues.en: places that made it at a particular moment in time.
cues.zh: 以及在某个特定时刻创造它的那些地方的延伸。

cues.en: And that's what The Simpsons is.
cues.zh: 《辛普森一家》就是这样一部作品。

cues.en: One of the purest and most raw expressions of social and political unrest,
cues.zh: 它是对社会和政治动荡最纯粹、最原始的expression之一，

cues.en: beautifully told and hilariously depicted.
cues.zh: 讲得漂亮，画得搞笑。

cues.en: And despite what it's become and how it's all ended,
cues.zh: 尽管它后来变成了这样，尽管一切都以那样的方式收场，

cues.en: I can't help be so glad that we got those early seasons.
cues.zh: 我还是忍不住为拥有那些早期季而感到无比庆幸。

cues.en: It was a show that shaped a generation and transformed entertainment as we know it, and I'm very very glad it did. But regardless,
cues.zh: 它塑造了一代人，也改变了我们熟知的娱乐方式，我非常非常高兴它做到了。但不管怎样，

cues.en: this has been the story of how the greatest show on Earth became just another sitcom.
cues.zh: 这就是地球上最伟大的剧集如何沦为又一部普通情景喜剧的故事。
